## Back to Research Themes

Return to the [Research Themes and Experiment Ledger](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}).

## Technical summary

Native audio is not one capability. Words, vocal delivery, environmental sound,
and identifying the title of a recording require different evidence. The current
evidence does **not** support turning native audio on for every question. It
does leave category-routed audio open: the clearest diagnostic improvements are
in prosody and non-speech sound, while exact music-title questions remain a
retrieval problem rather than a general-VLM guessing task.

## Why this theme matters

An automatic transcript can preserve spoken words but loses tone, music,
alarms, overlapping voices, and timing. A native-audio model can consume that
signal, but it may also distract from a visual or temporal question. Treating
all audio questions alike would hide that trade-off.

## Current working answer

Keep the 12-frame visual baseline as the default and the MiniCPM-o audio-off
path as the **Fast alternate**. Native audio is a **Routed candidate** for a
declared prosody or non-speech-sound question, not a global switch. Exact music
identification should abstain or use fingerprint/retrieval evidence rather than
ask a general VLM to invent a title.

## What has been tried

### Matched MiniCPM audio-on/off screen {#minicpm-audio-on-off}

- **Reason for testing:** learn whether adding the same clip's native audio to
  MiniCPM-o improves a matched visual path.
- **Tested condition and panel:** a 10-row pre-v2 gate compared MiniCPM-o 4.5
  with 12-frame native-video input, audio off versus audio on.
- **Observed result:** audio off was `0.300 / 0.586 / 0.414` (exact match /
  token F1 / METEOR), while audio on was `0.300 / 0.471 / 0.283`: the exact
  match tied and F1/METEOR changed by `-0.115 / -0.131`.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition** as a global audio-on policy.
- **What this rules out now:** enabling native audio by default for this
  MiniCPM version and 10-row gate.
- **What it does not rule out:** a matched specialist route for prosody,
  non-speech sound, or another model/prompt/panel.
- **Reconsider when:** a stratified, audio-off/audio-on comparison meets a
  predeclared target-stratum gain and visual/temporal-control non-regression.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

This was pre-v2 screening evidence, not part of frozen-30's four-condition
ranking. Its promotion rule also required non-speech wins, multilingual wins,
and no temporal/control loss; it did not pass. The [protocol-v2 report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md)
records the gate values and explicitly calls for a new controlled native-audio
test rather than assuming it helps.
</details>

### Failure-selected native-audio diagnostic {#failure-panel-native-audio}

- **Reason for testing:** determine whether native audio recovers known
  failures involving voice delivery, sound, music, and brief actions.
- **Tested condition and panel:** MiniCPM-o 4.5 with the same 12 frames, audio
  off versus full native audio, on 12 deliberately selected failures: two
  dialogue/prosody, four sound/music, four temporal-action, and two visual
  controls.
- **Observed result:** audio on was `4C/3P/5W` versus audio off `4C/4P/4W`.
  It improved emotional prosody, a popping sound, and instrument-family
  plausibility, but lost a bell and two temporal rows; its blind ordinal score
  rose from 4 to 6 on the first six audio-heavy rows and fell from 12 to 11
  overall.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Diagnostic signal** for category-gated
  native audio; **Not promoted under the tested condition** as a global switch.
- **What this rules out now:** treating this MiniCPM audio-on configuration as
  a better all-question policy on the failure-selected panel.
- **What it does not rule out:** native audio for declared prosody or
  non-speech-sound strata, a different audio-capable model, or an audio route
  with abstention.
- **Reconsider when:** a representative matched panel shows a target-stratum
  gain while preserving visual-control and temporal performance.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The first launch had a container-mount error before inference; the corrected
run completed all 12 requests. That operational repair is not evidence of
quality. This panel was selected from known failures, so it can diagnose
recovery behavior but cannot estimate full-test prevalence or rank systems.
See the [failure-panel report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/failure_panel_qwen36_audio_results_2026-07-24.md).
</details>

### Native audio with Qwen3-Omni {#qwen3-omni-native-audio}

- **Reason for testing:** check whether a larger joint audio/vision model can
  use native audio while holding the 12-frame visual evidence fixed.
- **Tested condition and panel:** a 10-row difficult, failure-selected panel
  compared Qwen3-Omni frames-only with the same frames plus native audio under
  a modality-neutral prompt.
- **Observed result:** the semantic diagnostic changed from `3C/3P/4W` to
  `5C/2P/3W`: prosody and non-speech sound improved from partial to correct,
  and one action improved from wrong to partial; both visual controls stayed
  correct. The unchanged strict run completed only 19 of 20 required outputs.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Diagnostic signal**; it is formally
  ineligible for promotion under the predeclared 20/20 completion gate.
- **What this rules out now:** promoting that incomplete strict run or calling
  native audio a new overall default from this ten-row diagnostic.
- **What it does not rule out:** a repaired, complete, blinded Qwen3-Omni
  comparison, or a category route whose gate is met on a representative panel.
- **Reconsider when:** terminal-output handling passes a sentinel check and a
  fresh full paired run completes 20/20 under one frozen contract.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

One complete answer was wrapped in a Markdown JSON fence and failed the
unchanged strict parser; a post-hoc semantic diagnostic cannot change that
eligibility outcome. The panel is selected and frame-based, so it is neither a
global ranking nor a complete native-video test. Model-specific gate details
are on [Models and Adaptation](research-models.{{< meta report-ext >}}#qwen3-omni-quality).
See the [quality-10 report](../../docs/experiments/2026-07-25-qwen3-omni-quality-10.md).
</details>

### Sound and music diagnostic boundaries {#sound-music-boundary}

- **Reason for testing:** distinguish non-speech sound recognition from speech
  transcription and exact music-title retrieval.
- **Tested condition and panel:** frozen-30 includes six non-speech
  sound/music rows; the failure panel additionally includes four selected
  sound/music failures.
- **Observed result:** no frozen-30 condition produced an exact match in the
  non-speech sound/music stratum. In the failure panel, native audio could
  recognize some sound character but produced plausible wrong music and bell
  answers; general VLMs did not establish exact-title retrieval.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Open hypothesis** for a dedicated sound
  route; exact music-title retrieval is **Not promoted under the tested
  general-VLM conditions**.
- **What this rules out now:** using ASR text as a substitute for non-speech
  audio or asking the current general VLMs to guess an exact composition title.
- **What it does not rule out:** an audio-event classifier, fingerprint lookup,
  or a provenance-safe music retrieval system that can abstain.
- **Reconsider when:** a route names its evidence source, abstention behavior,
  and target-stratum control before a matched evaluation.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

Frozen-30 is the stronger panel but has only six rows per stratum; the
failure-selected rows are diagnostic only. The [protocol-v2 report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md)
and [failure-panel report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/failure_panel_qwen36_audio_results_2026-07-24.md)
support this separation.
</details>

## What the evidence supports

- Speech text and native sound are complementary evidence types, not
  interchangeable routes.
- Current global audio-on diagnostics do not beat their audio-off controls.
- Prosody and non-speech sound are plausible specialist strata because two
  separate selected diagnostics show localized native-audio gains.
- Exact music-title questions require a retrieval-style hypothesis; no current
  general-VLM result validates confident title generation.

## What it does not rule out

- A negative global switch does not reject a quality-gated native-audio route.
- The selected panels do not estimate how often prosody, sound, or music occur
  in the 2026 evaluation set.
- The Qwen3-Omni diagnostic does not settle the quality of a complete run, a
  different prompt, or native temporal video input.
- Audio-event recognition is not established merely because a model generated
  a plausible sound label.

## Possible bugs, confounds, and audit gaps

- **Uncertainty:** the MiniCPM and Omni audio findings are on pre-v2 or
  deliberately selected panels, not representative prevalence samples.
- **Confirmed defect:** the Qwen3-Omni strict run had one parser-contract
  failure. It is a completion-gate defect, not proof that its semantic output
  is useless.
- **Uncertainty:** changing native audio can alter how a model allocates
  attention; a temporal regression need not mean the sound evidence was absent.
- **Audit gap:** the repository has route ideas and diagnostics, not a versioned
  evaluated audio router with abstention and route-level non-regression.
- **Audit gap:** the failure-panel report names localized audio gains and losses
  but does not retain a complete transition matrix for every audio-on/off row;
  that missing detail is not evidence of an execution bug.

## Open hypotheses and ideas

- Native audio improves prosody and non-speech sound when the question is
  explicitly routed, while it can hurt unrelated temporal or visual answers.
- A lightweight non-speech audio classifier can decide when to invoke a native
  audio model and otherwise abstain to an audio-off control.
- Music fingerprinting or retrieval can answer exact-title questions more
  reliably than a general VLM, provided it can abstain on weak matches.

## Cheapest valid next experiments

### Matched native-audio specialist panel

- **Hypothesis:** audio on improves prosody and non-speech sound more than
  audio off without degrading visual or temporal controls.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a frozen, label-blind panel with
  speech, prosody, non-speech, temporal, and visual-control strata.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** identical clips, frames,
  model, prompt, decoding, ordering, scoring, audio-off control, and frozen
  answers before labels load.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** advance a route only with a predeclared
  paired target-stratum gain and no worse than the declared temporal/control
  regression limit.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** a category route for
  the tested model and strata, not universal native-audio benefit.

### Non-speech classifier with abstention

- **Hypothesis:** a non-speech classifier can safely select native audio only
  when its signal is relevant.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a hand-reviewed, label-blind sound
  versus non-sound development slice with an audio-off/native-VLM control.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** version the classifier and
  threshold; hold visual evidence and downstream prompt fixed; record route,
  abstention, and fallback; freeze predictions before scoring.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** adopt only if routed end-to-end quality beats
  audio-off without route-level or aggregate non-regression failures.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** selection quality for
  that classifier and slice, not sound recognition in every genre.

### Exact-music fingerprint or retrieval route

- **Hypothesis:** a fingerprint/retrieval path with abstention answers exact
  music-title questions more reliably than a general VLM guess.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a provenance-approved music-title
  diagnostic with known-answer controls and no-match cases.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** freeze the fingerprint/index
  version and matching threshold; include audio-off and general-VLM controls;
  retain abstentions; score only after predictions freeze.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** advance only when exact retrieval improves
  the declared title cases and weak matches abstain rather than fabricate.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** the retrieval route's
  performance on its indexed catalog, not general music knowledge.
